Syntax reproduction: python3 -m py_compile reflect_prediction.py reflect_adapter.py duplicate_prediction.py duplicate_adapter.py.

Implementation: both signs and the pivot-axis adapter are evaluated in every cell. Select pair (positive,negative) for reflect or (positive,positive) for duplicate. Compute their FP32 mean, cast back to inherited adapter dtype, and build click tower rows [mean,mean,first,second]. One ordinary 4B tower call in both training/eval gives common native Dice support to early and late readouts at common state. Early selects the probability mean of the first two rows; late selects the last two. Both readouts execute in all cells; zero terms retain the unselected graph. Batch-statistic coupling means unselected tower support rows can still carry gradients; do not assert they have zero gradient. Auxiliary towers remain B and the BCE objective remains the sum of four unweighted losses on returned probabilities. All event fields, actions, task masks, padding, target and 100-event restrictions are untouched. Reflection changes only the coarse moment fed to the click adapter, not whole-history order. Other routes retain local/curvature/joint and axis information.

topics.title: 序列与字段的统一交互结构
topics.question: 怎样的信息流能使序列建模与字段交互共同演化，并在给定预算下改善预测效果或效率？
topics.hypothesis: 先汇聚再交互、逐层联合交互、并行交换或路由结构具有不同的信息瓶颈；依据诊断选择机制，允许完整重写网络，并与最接近的结构比较。

topics.title: Capacity allocation and measured prediction cost
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, can reducing or reallocating representation and interaction capacity preserve the stronger source click AUC while reducing parameter count and measured inference cost?
topics.hypothesis: The stronger source may have reducible or unevenly useful capacity. Starting from its frozen best, simple capacity reductions and matched-parameter reallocations should identify a smaller, faster configuration that preserves click AUC. Compare against the unchanged source and shared baseline under the same protocol; use replacement controls, matched training exposure, measured training and inference cost, and repetitions before claiming robust retention. Consistent AUC loss under capacity reduction, or an advantage explained by additional capacity or compute, would falsify the proposed efficiency benefit within the tested range. The compact summaries do not identify which components are redundant; component choices require inspection in the implementation phase.

topics.title: Historical feedback value beyond advertisement context
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and history policy, how much of the strongest joint model's click-AUC gain depends on observed historical actions, and does that dependence interact with task-conditioned history representation?
topics.hypothesis: Historical actions may contribute predictive information beyond advertisement and context content, with task conditioning determining its utility. Starting from the frozen joint best, compare action availability and task conditioning with factorial removal and matched-capacity replacement controls, preserving every original history-mask restriction and the training protocol. Retain the unchanged joint model, both source bests, context-only reference and shared baseline as utility controls; measure parameters, training and inference cost. A reproducible action-removal loss surviving replacement controls would support feedback utility; an interaction would support dependence on task conditioning. No loss, a capacity or optimization explanation, or failure to repeat would weaken that account. Neither source gains nor a single favorable contrast establish the mechanism.

topics.title: History-order utility in the strongest joint model
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does the supplied order of valid historical events improve click AUC beyond their content in the strongest joint model, and is any benefit justified by measured cost?
topics.hypothesis: The inherited joint history compression and task-conditioned representation may exploit predictive event order, but the supplied evidence does not establish this. Retain the unchanged starting model as the utility control and compare order-preserving and order-invariant treatments with matched-capacity replacements. Any permutation must keep event fields and historical actions aligned, transport each task's eligibility with its event, and preserve padding and every original history restriction. Use only supplied positions, without assuming timestamps, time gaps or unavailable events. Order-dependent predictive information would be supported by a reproducible advantage over controls trained under their corresponding order treatment. Equal or better order-invariant performance would falsify useful order dependence for the tested setting; sensitivity only to prediction-time permutations could instead reflect distribution shift. Separate order effects from capacity, optimization and compute through replacement controls, measured parameters and runtime, and reserved resources for attribution and repetition before assessment. This is an untested local hypothesis, with no novelty or mechanism-confirmation claim.

topics.title: Conditional utility of task-mask membership
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does task-mask membership improve click AUC beyond aligned historical item content and action codes in the strongest visible model, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topics.hypothesis: Task-mask membership may supply useful event assignment beyond item content and historical actions; the compact evidence does not establish this. Inherit the strongest visible trial unchanged as the utility control. Compare full membership use with a membership-blind representation and a counts-only replacement to distinguish event assignment from task-history frequency. Keep host mask construction, valid history, event order, aligned item fields and actions, target inputs, supervision and training exposure fixed; representation controls must not expose padded events or alter label construction. Use matched-capacity replacements and measure training and inference cost. A valid-history membership-permutation control should preserve per-task counts and joint membership patterns while disrupting their association with event content. Full membership failing to beat these controls would undermine its conditional utility; an apparent gain explained by capacity, cost or frequency would not establish useful event assignment. Repeat a discriminating comparison before claiming support, reserving resources for attribution and assessment. This question concerns representation use of masks, distinct from changing historical actions or auxiliary-gradient participation.

decisions.reason: After 24 current-topic trials, the best routing control reaches 0.657149 AUC; all three routing-enabled contrasts are lower (0.656578–0.656680). The stronger source reaches 0.660647 with fewer parameters (32.060M versus 32.274M) and lower measured inference time (24.46 versus 29.53 seconds). Switch to capacity/cost attribution from that source. These single-seed observations do not establish its mechanism or robustness; preserve the source and shared baseline as controls.

topic.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, can reducing or reallocating representation and interaction capacity preserve the stronger source click AUC while reducing parameter count and measured inference cost?
topic.hypothesis: The stronger source may have reducible or unevenly useful capacity. Starting from its frozen best, simple capacity reductions and matched-parameter reallocations should identify a smaller, faster configuration that preserves click AUC. Compare against the unchanged source and shared baseline under the same protocol; use replacement controls, matched training exposure, measured training and inference cost, and repetitions before claiming robust retention. Consistent AUC loss under capacity reduction, or an advantage explained by additional capacity or compute, would falsify the proposed efficiency benefit within the tested range. The compact summaries do not identify which components are redundant; component choices require inspection in the implementation phase.

decisions.reason: After 24 attempts, capacity reductions have not established AUC preservation: context8_item16 uses about 12% fewer parameters but loses 0.000553 AUC; uniform8 roughly halves parameters but loses 0.001530. Continue with a bounded transfer test on the stronger frozen joint best (0.663211 AUC, 32.108M parameters, 25.55s inference). Retain its unchanged version, recent10 and the original source as controls; match training exposure, control allocation comparisons for capacity, and repeat timing. Whether reductions preserve stronger-source AUC while lowering measured cost remains unresolved; failure on either criterion should end this branch. Single-seed performance does not confirm a mechanism.

Coupled item15 reduces parameters 4.75% versus its item16 control with observed AUC loss 0.0000583, and exceeds the matched-parameter native item15 control by 0.0018767 AUC. These single-seed contrasts justify deepening capacity allocation, but neither AUC preservation nor meaningful speedup is established: paired inference times are 23.918 versus 23.994 seconds. Retain unchanged source and matched-capacity controls; test repeatability and measured cost. Failure to preserve AUC or reduce inference cost would falsify the joint efficiency objective.

After 72 attempts, the current topic gains only 0.000055 AUC over entry; its smaller best is slower than the full16 replay. The joint-history best reaches 0.666754 AUC versus 0.660647 for context-only, but this does not attribute the gain to historical feedback. Switch to controlled feedback attribution, retaining source controls and measuring capacity and cost; single-seed differences remain provisional.

topic.question: Under the frozen inputs and history policy, how much of the strongest joint model's click-AUC gain depends on observed historical actions, and does that dependence interact with task-conditioned history representation?
topic.hypothesis: Historical actions may contribute predictive information beyond advertisement and context content, with task conditioning determining its utility. Starting from the frozen joint best, compare action availability and task conditioning with factorial removal and matched-capacity replacement controls, preserving every original history-mask restriction and the training protocol. Retain the unchanged joint model, both source bests, context-only reference and shared baseline as utility controls; measure parameters, training and inference cost. A reproducible action-removal loss surviving replacement controls would support feedback utility; an interaction would support dependence on task conditioning. No loss, a capacity or optimization explanation, or failure to repeat would weaken that account. Neither source gains nor a single favorable contrast establish the mechanism.

decisions.reason: Continue feedback attribution despite no utility gain over entry (-0.000509 AUC). Alignment improves AUC by 0.003045 with task conditioning and 0.003419 with shared representation; the interaction is -0.000375, provisionally favoring alignment in both settings rather than positive synergy. Equal parameter counts control nominal capacity; runs cost 375-383 seconds training and 29-30 seconds inference. Retain the unchanged entry as a utility control. Action-removal and matched-capacity replacement controls must distinguish feedback information from rotation artifacts; disappearance under those controls would undermine the explanation. Reserve the remaining budget for discriminating controls and repetition; single-seed contrasts do not establish a mechanism.

Task-conditioned variants exceed matched-parameter shared variants by 0.00164–0.00224 AUC; raw/scaled task variants are nearly tied. The topic best remains 0.000509 below entry, and recent inference costs are 29.6–30.5 seconds. Continue action-availability × task-conditioning attribution with mask-preserving removal and matched-capacity replacements, retaining unchanged entry and measuring runtime. Failure to improve over action removal would undermine feedback utility; disappearance under replacement controls would undermine action-specific attribution. Reserve confirmation resources: single-seed contrasts leave these mechanisms unresolved.

Task conditioning improves AUC over matched shared variants in both recent contrasts, but all four results trail the topic entry after 70 attempts. Historical-action utility remains unresolved. Continue attribution against the stronger joint reference with action-availability × task-conditioning controls, matched capacity and measured cost; transfer to that reference is unverified.

Recent history-mean click/shift contrasts differ by 0.00223 AUC with task conditioning and 0.00303 with sharing at equal parameter counts; these single-seed observations do not establish historical-action utility or its interaction with task conditioning. The topic best remains 0.000401 below its frozen entry. Deepen attribution with action-availability by task-conditioning controls and matched-capacity replacements, retaining the unchanged entry as a utility control and comparing measured runtime.

The strongest visible result reaches 0.668527 AUC with 32,192,421 parameters and 28.72s inference, but no supplied contrast isolates history order. topic.title: History-order utility in the strongest joint model
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does the supplied order of valid historical events improve click AUC beyond their content in the strongest joint model, and is any benefit justified by measured cost?
topic.hypothesis: The inherited joint history compression and task-conditioned representation may exploit predictive event order, but the supplied evidence does not establish this. Retain the unchanged starting model as the utility control and compare order-preserving and order-invariant treatments with matched-capacity replacements. Any permutation must keep event fields and historical actions aligned, transport each task's eligibility with its event, and preserve padding and every original history restriction. Use only supplied positions, without assuming timestamps, time gaps or unavailable events. Order-dependent predictive information would be supported by a reproducible advantage over controls trained under their corresponding order treatment. Equal or better order-invariant performance would falsify useful order dependence for the tested setting; sensitivity only to prediction-time permutations could instead reflect distribution shift. Separate order effects from capacity, optimization and compute through replacement controls, measured parameters and runtime, and reserved resources for attribution and repetition before assessment. This is an untested local hypothesis, with no novelty or mechanism-confirmation claim.

topic.title: Conditional utility of task-mask membership
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does task-mask membership improve click AUC beyond aligned historical item content and action codes in the strongest visible model, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topic.hypothesis: Task-mask membership may supply useful event assignment beyond item content and historical actions; the compact evidence does not establish this. Inherit the strongest visible trial unchanged as the utility control. Compare full membership use with a membership-blind representation and a counts-only replacement to distinguish event assignment from task-history frequency. Keep host mask construction, valid history, event order, aligned item fields and actions, target inputs, supervision and training exposure fixed; representation controls must not expose padded events or alter label construction. Use matched-capacity replacements and measure training and inference cost. A valid-history membership-permutation control should preserve per-task counts and joint membership patterns while disrupting their association with event content. Full membership failing to beat these controls would undermine its conditional utility; an apparent gain explained by capacity, cost or frequency would not establish useful event assignment. Repeat a discriminating comparison before claiming support, reserving resources for attribution and assessment. This question concerns representation use of masks, distinct from changing historical actions or auxiliary-gradient participation.

decisions.reason: Full-minus-counts AUC is +0.0000582 row-local and zero with uniform auxiliary weighting; neither exceeds inherited AUC 0.668961. These single-seed observations leave conditional membership utility unresolved. Continue with membership-by-auxiliary-weighting contrasts at the inherited model, retaining full, counts-only and membership-blind controls, frozen inputs/history policy and matched capacity. Recent runs cost 456–466 seconds at 32,192,421 parameters; reserve the remaining budget for attribution, repetition and measured runtime. No reproducible full-membership advantage over replacements would support closing this question; the current contrast does not establish a mechanism.
